title: Pinching Simulation Override
content: # **New in 2026.1** **** Temporarily overrides global and fabric simulation properties during pinching. **** ## **Location** To enable Pinching Simulation Override dialog: 1. In the 3D window, use the mouse to right-click an empty area, then select Simulation Properties. Alternatively, go to Settings > Simulation Properties. 2. Enable the Pinching Simulation Override checkbox. When Pinching Simulation Override is enabled, the Pinching Simulation Override dialog appears whenever a Pinching tool is activated in Simulation mode. ## **** ## **Operation** ### **Rest Shape** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Update Rest Shape** | Updates the Rest Shape using the current 3D state. **Reset Rest Shape** | Restores the Rest Shape to its original pattern-based state. **Selected Patterns / All Patterns** | Sets the scope to which the Rest Shape update or reset is applied. **Show Rest Shape Override** | Displays patterns with changed Rest Shapes in gray in the 3D window. ### **Simulation Properties** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Override Strength** | Sets how much Pinching Simulation Override is applied. 0 uses the original simulation properties, and 1 fully applies the override properties. **Global** | Adjusts the global simulation properties used when the override is fully applied. **Fabric** | Adjusts the fabric simulation properties used when the override is fully applied. The fabrics to override can be selected using checkboxes. **※ Note** * Update Rest Shape changes the reference shape that the simulation restores toward, helping maintain the edited shape during pinching. * Updating the Rest Shape causes the result to differ from the original pattern-based shape and area. Repeated updates can increase this difference. * Pinching Simulation Override is designed to support editing the base garment shape through pinching, not simulations driven by moving collision objects. * To maintain the edited shape in Animation Record, apply Solidify after pinching.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on using the new Pinching Simulation Override feature in version 2026.1 to temporarily adjust global and fabric simulation properties during pinching operations.

title: Seamline Rip
content: **New in 2026.1** Objective Location Create Seamline Rip Edit Seamline Rip Set Seamline Properties Produce Rip Result Restore the Ripped Area * * * ## Objective The **Seamline Rip Tool** allows part or all of a sewing line to be designated as a rip area, and simulates the effect of the actual fabric opening and fraying. After creating an **Seamline Rip** on a sewing line of a 3D garment or 2D pattern, adjust the **Rip** and **Fray** properties to create effects such as seam rupture, damaged garments, and worn fabric details. * * * ## Location * 3D Toolbar ▶ Seamline Rip * 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Rip * * * ## Create Seamline Rip ### **Partial Creation** A **Seamline Rip** can be created on a **Sewing Line**. 1. Select the **Seamline Rip Tool** from the **3D Toolbar**. 2. Move the mouse over the sewing line where the Rip object will be created on the 3D garment or 2D pattern. → A **Preview Point** appears at the position where creation is available. 3. Click on the sewing line to set the **Start Point**. → The **Start Point** is also displayed at the corresponding position on the **Paired Sewing Line**. 4. Move the mouse along the same sewing line. → A **Preview Line** is displayed from the **Start Point** to the current position. 5. Click another position on the sewing line to set the **End Point**. → A green **Rip object** is created between the **Start Point** and **End Point**. 6. The created **Seamline Rip** remains selected. → The **Seamline Rip** properties are displayed in the **Property Editor**. ### **Batch Creation** 1. Activate the **Sewing Tool** and select all Sewing Lines where Seamline Rips will be created. 2. Right-click to open the **Sewing Line Context Menu**. 3. Run **Add Seamline Rip**. 4. Select the **Edit Rip** tool and confirm that Seamline Rips have been created to fully cover the selected Sewing Lines. ※ Note: * **Seamline Rip** can only be created on a **Sewing Line**. A single **Rip object** can only be created within one **Sewing Line** and cannot continue across another connected Sewing Line. * When a Rip object is created by the user, a **Paired****Seamline Rip** is also created and synchronized on the opposite Sewing Line corresponding to the source Sewing Line. * However, the properties that control ripping can be set individually. A Rip object cannot be created multiple times on the same Vertex of the same Sewing Line. * * * ## Edit Seamline Rip Created Rip objects can be edited by adjusting their length, moving their position, deleting them, or editing their properties. 1. Select the **Edit Rip Tool**. 2. Select the Rip object to edit. → The **Start Point** , **End Point** , and **Line** of the selected Rip are highlighted. → The **Paired****Seamline Rip** is also displayed. 3. Drag the **Start Point** or **End Point** to adjust the length. 4. Drag the **Rip Line** to move its position along the same Sewing Line. 5. Release the mouse button to confirm the change. **※ Note** * When the length or position of a Rip is changed, subsequent simulation is performed based on the updated area. * If simulation is run after deleting a Rip, the previously ripped section is merged again. * * * ## Set Seamline Rip Properties When an **Seamline Rip** is selected, **Rip** and **Fray** properties can be set in the **Property Editor**. ### **Rip Properties** **Rip Properties** define the conditions for the specified **Seamline Rip** area to tear in real time in response to force applied during simulation. Name | Description ---|--- **Activate** | Enables the ripping effect of the Rip. When set to **On** , ripping occurs in real time once a certain force threshold is reached. **Restore on Deactivation** | When simulation is run after turning **Activate** Off, the previously ripped area is merged again while keeping the Rip object. **Rip Resistance** | **Rip Resistance** controls the seam’s resistance to tearing. It is calculated internally from Yield Strength, the force threshold at which damage begins, and Damage Rate, the rate at which damage accumulates over time. Lower values make the seam easier to tear; higher values increase its resistance to sustained force. ### **Fray Properties** **Fray Properties** are used to represent fabric wear or fraying around the outline of the ripped **Seamline**. Name | Description ---|--- **Preset** | Saves the Fray properties as a **ZFRAY** file so they can be reused. The Preset list is synchronized with the corresponding folder. Path: C:\Users\Public\Documents\MarvelousDesigner\New Assets\Fabric\Fray **Common** | **Activate** | Controls whether all Fray components are enabled. All other Fray elements are displayed only when this is turned on. It is recommended to keep this option enabled. **Generation** | **Fray Distance Threshold (mm)** | Defines the "Distress Region": when the two sides of the rip surface are below this threshold, it is considered a "Distress Region" rather than fully ripped. **Bridge Probability** | Probability that, within the "Distress Region" a fray will remain a bridge as a Loose Warp rather than be generated as a Fuzz. **Root Offset (mm)** | How far the root is offset into the edge it lives on. **Variation** | **Thickness Variation** | Randomness added to fray thickness. **Arch Variation** | Randomness added to "Arch" parameter in certain fray types. **Wavy Variation** | Randomness added to "Wavy" for certain fray types. **Gravity** | **Gravity Strength** | Sets the strength of the gravity effect. **Gravity Direction X** | X-direction for gravith. **Gravity Direction Y** | Y-direction for gravith. **Gravity Direction Z** | Z-direction for gravith. **Material** | **Use Fabric Material** | Apply the Fabric's material properties to all Fray objects. **Fuzz** | **Activate** | Sets whether to draw **Fuzz** on the screen. This works only when **Common > ****Activation** is turned on. **Basic** | **Density (/mm)** | How many frays to generate per millimeter? **Thickness (mm)** | Base thickness of the fray. **Coverage (%)** | Randomly thins out the thread generation. **Length (mm)** | Length of the generated fray. **Length Variation** | Defines how much the length parameter varies by. **Taper** | Defines the ending radius of the fray. **Taper Variation** | Amount of randomness added to the taper field. **Segments** | Maximum number of segments used to model the fray. **Orientation** | **Lean Probability** | Defines the likelihood that a fray will have the "lean" effect added. Basically a deform leaning the fray to the left with a strength depending on the internal value. **Lean Strength** | Lean strength, if a fray gets the lean effect, it will be blended with a constant direction (towards the other side of the rip, generated once at generation time). **Rotation (°)** | Rotates the strand about its generation axis. **Grain Angle (°)** | This is supposed to rotate the frays at an angle within the plane of the seam. **Eyelash Rolling** | Intended to give an eyelash curling effect, curling the entire fray geometry. **Curl** | **Curliness** | Defines how many times the fray tries to spiral. **Curling Width** | Defines how wide the spiral curve of the fray will get. **Damping Power** | Damp out the curvature at the end of the fray, **Spiral Noise Strength** | Strength of noise added to the angular curling of the fray. **Spiral Noise Frequency** | Frequency of the noise applied to the angular curling of the fray. **Radial Noise Strength** | Strength of the noise added to the radial curling of the fray. **Radial Noise Frequency** | Frequency of the noise added to the radial curling of the fray. **Height Noise Strength** | Strength of noise added to the spacing of segment knots. **Height Noise Frequency** | Frequency of noise added to the spacing of segment knots. **Clumping** | **Clumping Radius** | Number of strands per clump, should be an integer value. **Clumping Damping Power** | Clumping strength. **Material** | **Color** | Sets the base color of the fray strands. **Glossiness** | Controls the strength and sharpness of surface reflections. **Softness** | Controls the perceived softness of the fray strands. **Loose** | **Warp** | **Activate** | Sets whether to draw **Loose Warp** on the screen. This works only when **Common > ****Activation** is turned on. **Basic** | **Density (mm)** | Number of loose warp threads to generate per edge. **Thickness (mm)** | Base thickness of the fray. **Segments** | Maximum number of segments used to model the fray. **Shape** | **Asymmetry** | Asymmetry of the wavy fray. **Arch** | Arch amplitude of thread. **Wavy Strength** | Amplitude of the waves, centered on fray. **Frequency** | Frequency of the fray waves. **Material** | **Color** | Sets the base color of the fray strands. **Glossiness** | Controls the strength and sharpness of surface reflections. **Softness** | Controls the perceived softness of the fray strands. **Weft** | **Activate** | Sets whether to draw **Loose Weft** on the screen. This works only when **Common > ****Activation** is turned on. **Basic** | **Density (mm)** | How many loose wefts to generate per edge pair. **Thickness (mm)** | Base thickness of the fray. **Segments** | Maximum number of segments used to model the fray. **Shape** | **Asymmetry** | Asymmetry of the wavy fray. **Arch** | Arch amplitude of fray from the seam edge. **Wavy Strength** | Amplitude of the waves, centered on fray. **Frequency** | Frequency of the fray waves. **Material** | **Color** | Sets the base color of the fray strands. **Glossiness** | Controls the strength and sharpness of surface reflections. **Softness** | Controls the perceived softness of the fray strands. **Exposed** | **Generation** | **Density (/mm)** | Density of exposed weft parameters. **Exposed Weft Snapping Probability** | Probability with which an exposed weft will stay an exposed weft rathee than "snap" and become an exposed warp **Clumping** | **Clumping Radius (mm)** | World space distance along the seam that determines clumps (all strands within this distance will clump together). **Clumping Strength** | Strength of clumping effect **Weft** | **Activate** | Sets whether to draw **Exposed Weft** on the screen. This works only when **Common > ****Activation** is turned on. **Basic** | **Thickness (mm)** | Base thickness of the fray. **Segments** | Maximum number of segments used to model the fray. **Shape** | **Arch** | Arch controls the height of the arch formed by the exposed weft curves. **Asymmetry** | Asymmetry of the wavy fray. **Wavy Strength** | Amplitude of the waves, centered on fray. **Frequency** | Frequency of the fray waves. **Material** | **Color** | Sets the base color of the fray strands. **Glossiness** | Controls the strength and sharpness of surface reflections. **Softness** | Controls the perceived softness of the fray strands. **Warp** | **Activate** | Sets whether to draw **Exposed Warp** on the screen. This works only when **Common > ****Activation** is turned on. **Basic** | **Thickness (mm)** | Base thickness of the fray. **Segments** | Maximum number of segments used to model the fray. **Shape** | **Length (mm)** | Length of the generated fray **Length Variation** | Defines how much the length parameter varies by **Taper** | Defines the ending radius of the fray. **Taper Variation** | Amount of randomness added to the taper field. **Curl** | **Spiral Noise Strength** | Strength of noise added to the angular curling of the fray. **Spiral Noise Frequency** | Frequency of the noise applied to the angular curling of the fray. **Radial Noise Strength** | Strength of the noise added to the radial curling of the fray. **Radial Noise Frequency** | Frequency of the noise added to the radial curling of the fray. **Height Noise Strength** | Strength of noise added to the spacing of segment knots. **Height Noise Frequency** | Frequency of noise added to the spacing of segment knots. **Material** | **Color** | Sets the base color of the fray strands. **Glossiness** | Controls the strength and sharpness of surface reflections. **Softness** | Controls the perceived softness of the fray strands. **※ Note** * Fray is **viewport****-only** and cannot be exported as geometry. * **macOS** is not supported yet. * Fray is displayed when two patterns connected by a Seamline are ripped. Therefore, it is recommended to adjust the Fray property values after the Seamline Rip has been torn and the Fray is visible. * If you need to use Fray repeatedly, it is recommended to save the desired Fray settings as a **Preset file (*.zfray)** and reuse them. * The Fray shape can be adjusted by changing the property values even when simulation is not running. * * * ## Produce Rip Result During simulation, force above the threshold can be applied to tear the prepared **Seamline Rip** area. 1. Prepare a garment with a Rip applied. 2. Select the **Seamline Rip** object, then turn on **Activate** in the **Property Editor**. 3. Run simulation. 4. Apply tension to the sewing line using an external force such as **Pinching**. 5. When the tension satisfies the **Rip Resistance** condition, the sewing line is ripped. 6. Check the ripped result and the **Fray** expression. 7. While simulation is running, adjust the **Fray** properties to refine the visual result. **※ Note** * If the length or position of the Rip is changed, or if the Rip is deleted during simulation, the running simulation stops. * **Rip** and **Fray** property values can be changed during simulation. * If the result is not as intended, use the **Edit Rip Tool** to adjust the length or position, then run simulation again. * * * ## Restore the Ripped Area The ripped state can be restored to the original sewn state. 1. Select the **Seamline Rip**. 2. Check the **Restore on Deactivation** option. 3. Turn off **Activate**. 4. Run simulation. → The ripped sewing line is restored to its original state. **※ Note** * **Restore Rip** restores the ripped result while keeping the Rip object. * **Delete Rip** deletes the Rip object itself.
content_description: Discover the powerful new **Seamline Rip Tool** in 2026.1, designed to simulate realistic fabric damage and fraying effects on garments and patterns, allowing for detailed customization of ripped areas in your designs.

title: Customize Toolbar
content: **New in 2026.1** **Group Tools** **Rearrange Tools** **Open/Save** **Reset to Default** **** Customize and rearrange tool groups in the 2D and 3D toolbars for quicker access to the tools you use most. ### **Group Tools** 1. Right-click on the 3D or 2D toolbar and select **Group Tools**. → The Group Tools window opens. 2. Select the toolbar you want to edit (3D or 2D) from the upper-right corner of the Group Tools window. → The current tool group layout and order are displayed as they appear on the toolbar. 3. Drag a tool to a new position within the same group. → The tool order within the group is updated. → The tool placed at the top of the group becomes the default tool displayed on the toolbar. 4. Drag a tool to a different group. → The tool is moved to the selected group. 5. Drag a tool from a group into the empty space between groups. → The tool is separated from its current group and becomes a new group. 6. Click **OK** to apply the changes. → The toolbar reflects the configured groups and tool positions. **📝****Note:** Hide unused tools from the toolbar by clicking the ![Eye Off.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/59782795604505) **Hide** button next to each tool.**** ### [**Rearrange Tools**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/59637467539225-Customize-Toolbar#h_01J6H83GX4GW2AT7B952NFY29P) 1. Right-click on the 3D or 2D toolbar and select **Rearrange Tools**. → Tool rearrangement mode is enabled. 2. Drag a tool to the desired position. * Tools cannot be moved between the 3D and 2D toolbars. ### ### **Open/Save** Click the **Open** or**Save** button in the lower-left corner of the Group Tools window, or go to Main Menu > Save As/Open > **Tool Set**. → Toolbar group configurations can be saved to and loaded from a JSON file. ### **Reset to Default** Right-click the 3D or 2D toolbar and select Reset to Default. → The toolbar is reset to the default settings. **📝****Note:** Resetting the toolbar cannot be undone. We recommend saving the current configuration to a file before resetting.

title: Lacing
content: **New in 2026.0** **Define Path** **Edit Lacing** **** Automate the lacing process by guiding the lacing pattern and direction through designated holes. This tool eliminates manual intervention by automatically routing the cord and generating an editable pattern for further customization. **** #### **Define Path** 1. Select the **Lacing Tool** from the 2D Toolbar. 2. Click the **starting hole** where the lacing begins or where the cord is first inserted. 3. Click the **next hole** in your desired sequence. 4. Continue clicking holes until you reach the **last** or **exit hole.** **** 5. To complete the sequence, **double-click** the final hole or press **Enter**. 6. An **editable lace pattern** will automatically generate in the 2D window for further modifications. **** **※ Updated in 2026.1** #### **Edit Lacing** Edit the direction or curvature of an existing lacing without deleting and recreating it. 1. Select the **Edit Lacing Tool** from the 2D Toolbar. 2. Click an **existing lacing** in the 2D/3D window to select it. 3. In the dialog, adjust the direction or curvature using the **Reverse** or **Curvature** options. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/61502084361241)** * **Reverse** * A **reverse icon** will appear attached to your cursor. * Click a specific hole to flip the lacing direction at that point. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/61502084361241)** * **Curvature** * Use the slider to adjust the cord's arc. Increasing curvature helps stabilise simulation by preventing the cord from colliding with or clipping into nearby patterns. **** **📝 Note:** The generated lace is a standard pattern piece; you can independently edit its thickness, material, or physical properties in the Property Editor like any other garment part. **✨ Tip:** If the cord enters an eyelet from the wrong side in 3D, use the **reverse icon** to flip the orientation without redrawing the entire path.
content_description: Explore the new **Define Path** and **Edit Lacing** tools in 2026.0 to automate and customize your lacing patterns effortlessly, enhancing design precision without manual intervention.

Place an Avatar in the 3D window. The Avatar Editor is accessible only when the avatar is in the 3D window. 2. Select the tool/menu indicated above under Location. → Avatar Editor window will appear. 3. Adjust the properties for the properties below. There are separate tabs for Avatar Size, Measure, Arrangement, Fitting Suit, and IK Joint. ### # Avatar Size Avatar size allows you to create a custom-size avatar with your own measurements. The Marvelous Designer Avatar Editor is powered by real body scan data to help you create realistic body shapes, whether you have a complete size specification or not. ### #### **Size:** Option | Description ---|--- Size | Custom / Presets | Select an Avatar size from the presets, or create an avatar with your desired size by inputting detailed measurements. From the dropdown, presets include standard sizing such as Curvy, Straight, Petite Curvy, Petite Straight, Plus Curvy and Plus Straight for women, and size 34 to 52 Standard for men. Additional size measurements can be added and entered in the "Set Details" from the gear icon. Avatar Name (.avs) | Select the Avatar file. Units of measurement | Select from Millimeter, Centimeter, Inch, Feet & Inch. Set Details (gear icon) | By clicking this icon, you can select and activate currently hidden size measurements. When checked on, they will become available in the Size section for editing. Show all Measurements (list icon) | By clicking this icon, you can view active and hidden size measurements that are not displayed in the editor window. If the measure is not checked on in the Set Details it will be visible, but not editable. Width / Height | The Width/Height categories allow you to select what you want the key measures to be for your size, and Marvelous Designer will then automatically generate a proportionate body shape based on these key measures. For example, if Under Bust and Total Height are selected here, circumference, height, and length measures below will be automatically created or slightly adjusted to maintain a proportional body shape. Link (default) | Size editing for Marvelous Designer avatars is algorithm-based, and by default, measures are linked to help you create a proportional body shape based on real human body scan data. Unlink | You can unlink the proportional editing by clicking the icon to deactivate it. When unlinked, any changes to the key Width/Height measurements will not affect the lower measurements. #### **Shape:** Option | Female | Male | Kid | Baby ---|---|---|---|--- Shape | Hand & Head | Hand | O | O | X | X Head | O | O | O | X Crotch | Width | O | O | X | X Volume | O | O | X | X Hip | Dips | O | O | X | X Volume | O | O | X | X Breast | Shape | O | X | X | X Space | O | X | X | X Height | O | X | X | X ### **Custom Avatar Size (recommended workflow)** 1. Go to Avatar > Avatar Editor to open the editor. Load the Avatar *.AVT and ensure it is the version you want to apply your size to. 2. If you are editing from an existing *.AVS file, click the open icon to select your file. When open, the avatar measures will be displayed in the 3D window. Measures that can be moved will appear as black dotted lines, and non-editable measures will be grey dotted lines. 3. Before entering size data in the editor window, ensure the desired values are available. If not, click the Set Details button to add them and Exit to go back to the main editor. For optimal results, it is recommended to activate only the measurements that you have. 4. Once you have your avatar and desired measures, select your key measures for Width / Height and enter your values. It is recommended to keep the default Link option on, but if desired, click the icon to unlink. 5. Now enter your desired measurements in circumference, height, and length. Note that when linked, Marvelous Designer will make slight automatic adjustments to maintain a proportional body shape. ※Note: When developing categories such as gloves, intimates, and headwear, you have additional options to adjust the head, hands, crotch, and bust to suit your needs. 6. Press Save to save your custom Avatar. After creating a custom size, you have the option to save the size only (*.AVS) or as an Avatar (*.AVT). The steps to modify the measurements of an Avatar are the same whether saving an *.AVT or an *.AVS file. The only difference is the way you open the file. #### **File Format** File name | Description ---|--- Avatar (.AVT) | The *.AVT is a Marvelous Designer native format, which contains all the information related to Avatars, including the model, skeleton rig, sizing, pose, motion, accessories, bounding volumes, and arrangement points. Avatar Size (.AVS) | The *.AVS format contains avatar size information. The Avatar file must be loaded before opening an *.AVS size file. The *.AVS format does not contain any avatar, only size information. ※Note: It is not possible to mix *.AVS files between avatars of different versions, age, or gender. The *.AVS file is only compatible with the avatar on which it was originally created. For example, if you created an *.AVS file using a female V2 Avatar, this will only apply to the female V2 Avatar. Saving in .AVS You can connect the folder you saved to your library and click-drag your different sizes on the avatar of your project file. You can open an .AVS file, using the Folder Icon next to Save in the Avatar Editor. Saving in .AVT If you want to add a custom Avatar in the workspace, open from File ▶ Open ▶ Avatar. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) # Measure You can use 6 types of avatar tape that allow you to create free measures, circumference, linear, and height measurements. Please see the [**Measure manual**](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358154578585-Avatar-Measure-above-ver-10) for additional Measure information. All added measurements can be viewed and renamed in the Measure tab. ※Note: The difference between ‘Basic’ and ‘Surface’ is whether the measure will follow the curvature of the avatar's body or follow a direct line around the widest points. The Basic Tapes are most akin to methods of measuring the body with soft measuring tape, whereas ‘Surface’ will measure along the curved surface of the body. #### **Measure:** Option | Description ---|--- Measure | Name | The default name appears after creating a new measure. Double-click on the text to rename. Delete | Delete the selected Measure. ※Note: You can also use the Edit Measurement tool to select the Tape Measure in the 3D Window and hit either the Backspace or Delete key. Fit to Avatar | Re-fit the measurements when changing its Pose or loading another Avatar's joints. Open | Open a *.MEA file created with other Marvelous Designer Avatars. Save | Save the measurements in *.MEA format to open with other Marvelous Designer Avatars. ※Note:.MEA files should be applied to the same model in the same version. Measurement Type | Toggle the Measurement Type between Basic and Surface to update the type without needing to recreate the measurement. Measurement Information | Measurement Information given is either Tape or Circumference. Basic Length | Check the value when measured with the Basic Measurement tool. Surface Length | Check the value when measured with the Surface Measurement tool. Show | Toggle on or off to show or hide the selected measurement in the 3D Window. Show Length | Toggle on or off to show or hide the selected measurement in the 3D Window. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) # Arrangement Edit, add or delete any of the Bounding Volumes or Arrangement Points in the Arrangement tab. Please see the [Arrangement manual](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/sections/47114831810969) for additional information on how to use Bounding Volumes and Arrangement Points. You can rename any Bounding Volume and Arrangement Point with "NAME_1_L", "NAME_1_R" to maintain symmetry. All arrangement points apart from the Avatar's body are symmetrically set by default. #### **Bounding Volume:** Option | Description ---|--- Board | Name | You can double-click to rename the default name. Add | A new Bounding Volume called “PAN” will be added at the bottom of the list. Delete | Deleted the selected Bounding Volume Reset Bounding Volumes | Reset to the original position Open | Open a pre-saved *.PAN file Save | Save the created *.PAN file to use with other avatars. Joint Name 0 | Set the beginning location of the Joint (X-ray) Joint Name 1 | Set the end location of the Joint (Show Avatar Joint) Height | Set the height Radius X (mm) | Set the horizontal radius Radius Y (mm) | Set the vertical radius Hands/Feet | Toggle on to extend BV's length to Avatar's hands or feet, respectively #### **Point:** Option | Description ---|--- Placement | Name | You can double-click to rename the default name. Add | A new arrangement point named “Arrangement Point” will be created at the bottom of the list. Note that the point is unassigned by default, and you will need to select the BV and X Y positions in the steps below. Delete | Delete the selected Arrangement Point. Open | Open an *.ARR file; this can be used to apply Arrangement points to an *.OBJ avatar. Save | Save as an *.ARR file and open on another Avatar. Note: Some readjustment may be needed when applying to another avatar. Arrangement BV | Selects the Bounding Volume where the Arrangement Point is to be placed. X | Moves the Arrangement Point left and right. Y | Moves the Arrangement Point up and down. Offset | Sets the distance between the Avatar and the Arrangement Point. Wrap Direction | Wrapping can be set to up or down and will determine the direction of the pattern wrap when placed on the Arrangement Point. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) # Fitting Suit 1. Draw lines on the avatar according to the indicated position below. 2. Create the circumference line on the avatar's position following the image. • The pattern of the fitting suit is displayed. • The circumference line on both sides is automatically created symmetrically. 3. After creating all the circumference lines, click the Drape Fitting Suit button. • The fitting suit is draped. Adjust the fitting in the 3D window if needed. Option | Description ---|--- Fitting Suit | Auto Create Fitting Suit | Click this icon to create a fitting suit automatically. If the avatar is not created properly, we recommend creating it manually. Create Symmetric Tape | Toggle on and off to create the draw line symmetric or not symmetric. Delete | Delete the drawing line. Reset | All drawing lines will be deleted. Save | Save as an *.AVT file. **![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438255194649) ** # IK Joint Use IK joint mapping with various avatars to achieve natural movement while ensuring seamless compatibility for motions and poses across all avatars. The avatar must have properly defined joint points. Rigging must include key joints such as shoulders, elbows, wrists, pelvis, knees, and ankles. Joints are categorized into required and optional, and you must map all required joints to ensure proper IK setup. ※ Note: The FBX file must not contain joints with duplicate names, and IK mapping may not apply correctly for creatures or quadruped avatars with non-human structures. Operation | Description ---|--- Open / Save | You can manage the IK data mapped to the avatar as a file. Click Open / Save icon at the top right to open or save IK data as a .iks file. ※Note: IK files are only compatible between avatars that have been mapped. Auto Mapping | If the avatar meets the following conditions, click Auto Mapping at the top right to apply automatic mapping. • If each joint name of the avatar matches that of the Marvelous Designer avatar. • If the avatar is from one of the following platforms: Daz 3D, Adobe Mixamo, Reallusion Character Creator, or Unreal Engine MetaHuman. Set T-Pose | Set the avatar in a T-pose to ensure proper compatibility with Marvelous Designer avatar pose and motion files apply correctly. Adjust the avatar’s joints directly to a T-pose using the gizmo in the 3D window. If the avatar is already in a T-pose, this step can be skipped. Click Set T-Pose button. Reset Pose | If T-Pose is set correctly, this button activates, allowing you to check the Set T-pose when clicked. After adjusting the pose during IK mapping, click this button to revert the avatar to the set T-pose. ****
content_description: The Avatar Settings page provides users with comprehensive tools to customize and adjust avatar size, measurements, arrangement, fitting suits, and IK joint setups for enhanced realism and accuracy in their designs.

title: [Tips&Tricks] Discover Better Workflow with Marvelous Designer and Unreal Engine
content: Through our collaborative efforts, we’re excited to introduce two new features for our community: the LiveSync plugin and USD export simulation data. In this article, we’ll explore how these powerful tools can elevate your workflow. Both the**LiveSync plugin** and **USD Export for Simulation Data** are tailored for users who frequently toggle between Marvelous Designer and Unreal Engine, but each serves a different purpose. * **LiveSync Plugin** : The feature is primarily aimed at simplifying the tedious import and export process. mesh, materials, skeletal animations, and geometry caches can all be imported and exported with just one click. * **USD Export Simulation Data** : Specifically designed to work with Unreal Engine 5.4's updated **Chaos Cloth** feature, this tool enables real-time simulation effects, translating complex clothing physics from Marvelous Designer directly into Unreal Engine. Let’s dive into how these tools enhance the design and animation workflow by walking through a case study featuring a fairy character animation sequence. ![Cenimetics_cc03_Still001.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438057410201) ## **Designing the Fairy Garment in Marvelous Designer** Before we jump into Unreal Engine, let's explore how we crafted the fairy's outfit in Marvelous Designer. ** ** **1\. Starting with a Simple T-Shirt Base** Marvelous Designer offers multiple ways to begin garment creation. For this project, we started by dragging a T-shirt pattern into the 2D window as a base. With the **Style Line tool,** we could quickly split and modify the T-shirt into a completely different style by adjusting the pattern directly in the 3D window, with real-time updates reflected in the 2D pattern. ![StyleLine_merged.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437978960409)**2\. Layering and Fabric Simulation** Marvelous Designer excels in simulating multi-layered garments. For the fairy outfit, we duplicated the underskirt pattern and added lace detail using internal lines. Each layer contributes to the garment’s dynamic, three-dimensional look. To simulate different fabric properties, we added a Muslin fabric preset from Marvelous Designer’s library of 77 fabric types, which changes the folds and flow of the skirt during simulation. ![08.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438009386649) **3\. Creating Petal Patterns and Pleating Effects** Using the Polygon Tool, we traced petal shapes for the skirt from a photo, then applied accordion pleat effect with the Internal Polygon Tool and Pleat Tool. The result was an elegant, multi-layered skirt with beautiful texture and movement. Thanks to Marvelous Designer's new PBR Texture Generator, we were also able to auto-generate texture maps (normal, opacity, metalness, displacement) with a single click, further enhancing the realism.![flower_paddle.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438009738777) ![06.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438009893657) **4\. Adding Ruffles and Topstitching**** **For the finishing touch, we created ruffles by sewing longer pattern edges onto shorter ones. And using the**Topstitch Tool** , we added stitching details that elevated the garment’s realism. ![TopStitch.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438058599321) After completing the garment design and the initial simulation in Marvelous Designer, we move on to caching the animation. ## **Animation Caching** First, using the **Pin Tool** , we secure certain parts of the garment to the character model by double-clicking the edge lines of the pattern pieces, quickly pinning the entire line. The **Tack Tool** is another way we can constrain the fabric to the model, while also allowing for length adjustments that control the distance between the fabric and the model. To cache the animation, we change the simulation preset to **Animation** , reduce the gravity value and increase air damping to simulate a floating, fairy-like effect. When all settings are in place, we click **Record** to start recording the animation cache. This cache will store all the necessary animation data, which can later be exported to Unreal Engine with full fidelity, preserving all simulation effects.** ** ## ![MD_Sim.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438058798361)**Calla Lily Creation** The vegetation in the scene is also modeled and simulated using Marvelous Designer. During the animation recording process, we can adjust the position and angle of the wind in real-time to create these natural dynamic effects. Marvelous Designer’s keyframe editing tool allows us to create perfect looping animations without frame skips—ideal for in-game sequences. Similar to video editing tools, we can cut layers and move layers horizontally. Copy the first frame and paste it at the end of the animation. The last frame of the animation blends into the first frame, creating a perfect cycle animation.** ** ![CalaLily.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438058959257) Once the animation was complete, both the fairy's garment and the calla lily were imported into Unreal Engine using the LiveSync Plugin, which maintains the accuracy of materials, animations, and textures during the transfer. ## **Transfer to Unreal Engine with LiveSync** Now that the fairy’s garment is complete, it’s time to bring the animation into Unreal Engine using the **LiveSync plugin**. After Install and Activate LiveSync, ensure that Marvelous Designer is running, then open the **LiveSync Editor** in Unreal Engine, and click the “Update” button.** ** ![LiveSync.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437980377625) The scene in Marvelous Designer is imported into the LiveSync Editor. In the editor, we can see that the shader balls have been automatically created based on the fabrics assigned in Marvelous Designer. We can also activate Unified Material; by clicking update again, the plugin will generate unified materials based on UV coordinates.![calalily_02.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438026338969)The capabilities of the **LiveSync plugin** aren’t limited to importing. MetaHuman characters, or any skeletal meshes, can be exported to and from Unreal Engine. Making it easier to create and simulate clothing for your characters. With all assets successfully imported, we used Unreal Engine’s **Sequencer** to animate and render the final scene. The fairy’s clothing, wings, and environment elements like calla lilies were all modeled and simulated in Marvelous Designer before being synchronized with Unreal Engine via the **LiveSync plugin**. ![light.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438011161625) ## **Leveraging Chaos Cloth with USD Export** **![gameplay_01.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437994671641)**The LiveSync plugin is suitable for rendering animations, creating videos, and cinematics using Unreal Engine. It can also be used to import environmental assets from Marvelous Designer (such as the calla lilies in this scene). But for users seeking real-time fabric simulation, Marvelous Designer’s**USD Export Simulation Data** is an invaluable asset, especially when paired with Unreal Engine’s **Chaos Cloth**. Let’s break down the process:** ** ![S01.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438060052249) **Optimizing for Chaos Cloth** : The fairy’s garment, with its complex layering, needed to be optimized before importing into Unreal Engine. By splitting the dress into three parts—skinned mesh, simulation mesh, and render mesh. ![05.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438043457817)**Auto-Retopology** and **Rigging** : The garment that does not need to participate in the simulation is skinned to the character’s body. The close-fitting garment does not need to participate in the simulation. Using Marvelous Designer’s **EveryWear Toolkit** , we performed automatic retopology and rigging. EveryWear is an automatic optimization toolkit for virtual clothing in games. Marvelous Designer's Quad Optimize option can achieve auto retopology. And with the EveryWear tool, we can reduce the polygon count. Rigging feature is also a part of EveryWear tool set. We can first specify the maximum number of influencing joints. Unreal Engine supports a maximum of 8 joints, so we set it to 8. Click 'Apply,' and the weights of the body mesh will automatically be copied to the garment. The skin weight can be painted and smooth using the brush tools. And we can use Hammer Tool and Repair brushes from the sculpting toolset to fix any intersections. ![Retpop.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438027448729)![Rigging.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438032351769) The primary challenge with this fairy's dress is that the petal skirt has too many layers, making it heavy and complex. The approach we used to optimize the skirt was to represent the multiple layers through textures instead of geometry. First, we split the skirt into two parts and unfolded it. Then, we created a simplified proxy model and used an orthographic view to render different AOV channels as texture maps. This significantly simplified the geometry, while the textures gave the illusion of layered complexity. ![04.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438060833689)![04 copy.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437995843737) (The left image shows the skirt unfolded in Marvelous Designer, and the right image illustrates how these layers are represented using textures.) ## **Optimizing Polygon Count** To further optimize the model, we need to reduce the polygon count. One way to do this is by increasing the particle distance in Marvelous Designer. When simulating fabric in 3D, random triangles tend to create more natural-looking folds. Using triangular meshes instead of quads works well with Chaos Cloth in Unreal Engine, so there’s no need to retopologize or convert to quads. Simply increasing the particle distance value will reduce the number of faces. Another important factor is increasing the collision thickness, which creates more separation between fabric layers. In this case, the collision thickness was increased from the default 2.5 mm to 5 mm for better results in Chaos Cloth.** ** ## ![CollisionThickness_03.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438032993177)**Exporting the USD File ** Once the model is optimized, we can export the USD file. Uncheck the option to export all avatars, select multiple objects in the export settings, and enable the "thick" option and unified UV coordinates. Crucially, ensure that the **Include garment simulation data** option is enabled. This will preserve all the physical properties assigned in Marvelous Designer, such as shrinkage and collision settings, so they can be read by Unreal Engine’s Chaos Cloth. ![SimulationProp \(1\).png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438033211929) ## **ClothAsset Setup in Unreal Engine** Back in Unreal Engine, we need to create a **ClothAsset**. Import the USD file exported from Marvelous Designer and select the skeletal mesh, which was also imported using the Marvelous Designer LiveSync plugin. This process skins the clothing to the character. In the preview scene, make sure to select the same skeletal mesh again.** ** ## **Painting Weights for Maximum Distance** Next, we’ll paint weights for the maximum distance property. It controls which parts of the fabric will participate in the simulation. Areas painted with 0 value represent regions that will not be simulated and are instead skinned directly to the character’s body. Use a smooth brush to create a gradient effect for the weights. You can paint weights in either the 2D or 3D views. If working in 2D, the layout and arrangement of the patterns are identical to what we see in the 2D window of Marvelous Designer. To make it easy for weight painting, make sure to pay attention to the layout of the patterns before exporting the USD file. The pattern pieces should not be too close together or have any overlapping. After painting the weights, click 'Accept' to preview the simulation results.** ** ![03.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438013248537) The weight values we painted can be adjusted using the **SimulationMaxDistanceConfig** node, which controls the highest and lowest weight values. Lowering the maximum value can further optimize the simulation. ## ## **Fabric Physical Properties ** The next three nodes are used to define the physical properties of the fabric. Normally, adjusting fabric properties is the most complex part of cloth simulation, but since we exported the physical properties from Marvelous Designer, this step becomes much simpler. By enabling the arrow icon on each parameter, we can directly use the fabric properties imported from Marvelous Designer.** ** ![SimData.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437996767769) Additionally, a clothing icon next to the nodes allows us to use the weight map generated in Marvelous Designer. Different fabric presets were applied to different patterns in Marvelous Designer, and the weight map is automatically exported with the USD file. ![SimData02.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438029196185) To enable the clothing to collide with the character’s body, we need to create a physics asset. This asset should be added to the **SetPhysicsAsset** node in Unreal Engine. ## ![PhysicsAssets.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438062365977)**Other Key Nodes for Cloth Simulation** * **SimulationCollisionConfig** : Controls fabric thickness and friction. Enabling the arrow icon will use values imported from Marvelous Designer. * **Self Collision** : Disabled by default for optimization. Enabling it will allow basic self-collision using spheres. Or use the more precise but more costly collisions through the **SimulationSelfCollisionConfig node.** * **SimulationSolverConfig:** This node manages global settings for the solver. Increasing the number of iterations strengthens the stiffness of constraints, but increases CPU load. Adjust the **Substep** value to improve collision accuracy at the cost of higher CPU load. Both settings must be optimized for performance and accuracy. You can also add aerodynamic effects to the simulation. By introducing wind fields, the clothing will move naturally during idle animations, making the character appear more lifelike. ## ## **Level of Detail (LOD) Settings** The final part of the preset involves configuring **LOD (Level of Detail)** settings. Different LODs will activate based on the camera’s distance from the character. The physical properties we configured earlier are connected to the top collection. A **Remesh** node is added to the middle LOD collection to reduce mesh density. The bottom collection, connected directly from the skinning node, doesn’t include dynamic simulation. If we want fabric simulation to be active all the time during gameplay, this collection can be removed.** ** ![02.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438034423193) ## ## **Merging the Simulation and Render Meshes** If a proxy model was used for simulation, we need to remove it as the render mesh using a**Delete Elements** node. Then, import a detailed render mesh, either as a static mesh or through a USD import node. Then use the **Merge Cloth Collection** node to combine the simulation mesh with the new render mesh.** ** ![RenderMesh.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438062736025) ## ** Final Setup in the Character Blueprint** In the character’s blueprint, add a**Chaos Cloth Component** and parent it to the character. Select the cloth asset we just created and adjust the position and rotation parameters if necessary. Compile and save the blueprint.** ** ![Character.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438048068761) Now, the clothing has real-time fabric simulation properties and will react naturally in the game environment. ![Still.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438048200601)Whether you’re creating cinematic sequences or in-game assets, the combination of Marvelous Designer’s **LiveSync plugin** and **USD Export Simulation Data** delivers a seamless, efficient workflow. The tools allow for rich, detailed simulations and quick iterations, significantly enhancing productivity. ![01.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438030245913)To explore these tools for yourself, the fairy model and garment are available for free download on our official [CONNECT store](https://connect.clo-set.com/). These files are intended for educational use and cannot be used for commercial purposes.
content_description: Discover how our new LiveSync plugin and USD export simulation data can streamline your design and animation workflow between Marvelous Designer and Unreal Engine, enhancing your creative projects with real-time simulation and simplified asset management.

title: Merge Symmetric Patterns
content: ### Objective Merge symmetric Patterns into a single Pattern. ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern Outline) ▶ Merge ### Operation 1. Navigate to 2D toolbar and select Edit Pattern tool. 2. Right click on the Pattern outline of either symmetric Pattern and follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern Outline) ▶ Merge → The symmetric Patterns are merged into a single Pattern as their Linked Editing function is removed. ※ Note: When there is any point on the selected segment to merge Patterns, the Patterns cannot be merged.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users on how to merge symmetric patterns into a single pattern using the Right Click Pop-Up Menu in the editing tool.

title: Merge
content: ### Objective Merge two Patterns in to a single Pattern. ### Location #### Pattern Outline Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern #### Sewing Line Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ### Operation #### Pattern Outline 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Select two Pattern outlines which two Patterns are to be merged accordingly. ※ Note: When the Patterns are symmetrically linked, select the Pattern outline of the either Pattern. 3. Right click on the selected Pattern outlines to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Merge. → The selected two Patterns are merged based on the selected Pattern outlines. → The original Pattern outlines are changed to Baselines. #### Sewing Line 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing 2. Right click on the Sewing Line which the Patterns are merged accordingly. Then, select Merge. → The two Patterns sewn with the selected Sewing Line are merged based on the selected Sewing Line. → The original Pattern outlines are changed to Baselines.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for merging two pattern outlines and their corresponding sewing lines into a single cohesive pattern.

title: Custom View
content: ### Objective Easily open and save custom view of the 3D window at your convenience. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Custom View Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Custom View ### Operation #### Create 1. Rotate the 3D Window as desired. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Custom View Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Custom View →The Custom View window appears. 3. title: 3D File (FBX) Import/Export
content: ### Objective Import a file's Geometry, Material, Joint, and Camera Animation information in the FBX file format (ver2.2.0). ### Location #### Import FBX Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ FBX #### Export FBX Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ FBX ### Operation #### Import FBX 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ FBX → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click OK. → The Import FBX window appears. 3. Select the settings and click OK. → The FBX file is imported based on the setting. Load Type | Open | All existing objects will be removed, leaving the imported FBX file only. ---|---|--- Add | Add a FBX file, keeping the existing objects. Auto Create Fitting Suit | For humanoid avatars only, a Fitting Suit is automatically created in the import process. Object Type | Avatar | Import a FBX file as an Avatar type. \- Objects imported as an Avatar type can be muti-selected. Trim | Import a FBX file as a Trim type. \- The object will pass through the clothing while Simulation is on, as the Trim type cannot collide with clothing. \- Set the collide option for a Trim type on the Property Editor by toggling on the Collision check-box. \- Select an trim object and toggle on the Glue icon on the gizmo to attach the object to clothing. \- Toggle on the Scale icon on the gizmo to scale the size of an object. Scene & Props | Import FBX file in Scene & Props format. \- You can use the Collision menu in the property window. Object | Camera | Toggles whether the Camera data or Camera Animation data is imported Joint Animation | Toggles whether the Joint Animation date is imported. Cache Animation (mc) | Toggles whether the Cache Animation data is imported. Automatically Add Arrangement Points | For humanoid avatars only, arrangement points are automatically generated in the import process. Scale | Input the Specific Value or Choose Measure. Axis Conversion | Modifying Object's Axis direction.(ver. 12.2) Translation | Align Bottom to Ground | When an object is placed below the ground, toggle on Align Bottom to Ground check-box to place the object imported above ground. Option | Move Garment to Start Position | Move the garment to the starting frame of the imported motion. #### Export FBX 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ FBX → The Save File window appears. 2. Designate the file saving path and file name, and then click OK. → The Export OBJ window appears. 3. Select the settings as needed and click OK. → The file is exported as a FBX file based on the setting. Object | Select an Avatar (ver 6.1) Select the avatar to be exported. ※ Note: The selected avatar is saved with its rigging data. You can exclude it as desired. Select All Avatars (ver. 12.2) \- All existing avatars will be exported. ---|--- **Single Object** Exports the selected object as a single object. | **Multiple Objects** Exports the selected object as multiple objects. **Un-Weld** Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. ※ Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version 2.3.0 (ver2.3.0). | **Weld** Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns (ver2.3.0). **Thin** Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. ※ Note: * When an object is exported as a single object, its texture is exported as a whole even when its sides (front, back, and side) have different textures (ver5.0.0.) | **Thick** Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. ※ Note: * The thickness can be exported when Pattern Mesh is Quadrangular (ver2.3.0.) * Each side's texture is exported individually when an object's front, back, side have different textures (ver5.0.0.) Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. ※Note: Unified Texture (ver3.1.0). Export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. | Image File | Designate file saving path and file name. Add numbers behind the file name as below: ‘File Name_0’, ‘File Name_1’. ---|--- Texture Size | Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 512 ~ 8192 Pixel Fill Texture Seams | Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. ※ Weld Turned Sewing Lines (ver 2026.0) Even when the Sewing Line Type is set to Turned, you can still merge vertices for export. Option | Joint Animation: | Saves the animation data that was originally imported with the FBX file. **※ Changes in ver 2026.0** \- Renamed to **Avatar Joint Animation.** \- When **Bake Animation** is activated, keys are generated for every frame and exported. Cache Animation (MC) | Saves the cache data along with the recorded Garment Animation. **※ Changes in ver 2026.0** \- Renamed to **Garment Animation (MCX).** \- **Avatar Cache Animation (MCX)** can now be exported separately. Scale | Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from “Unit in file to import” is selected. Axis Conversion | Changes the directions of each axis of the object. Animation | Entire Region | Exports the entire range where animation keys are set. Play Region Only | Exports only the animation within the specified playback range. File | File Type: Select between Binary or Ascii file type. * Binary: The file is saved in binary and cannot be opened by users. * Ascii: The file is saved as text and can be opened by users. Relative Texture Image File Path: Saves the texture image name without a texture image file path. Texture images are saved in the same folder as the FBX file, for automatic import. Absolute Texture Image File Path: Saves the file path that contained the texture images as the texture file path. If the texture image file path is changed, texture images cannot be imported. Save With Texture Files (.zip): Exports the .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. ※ Note: 1. FBX SDK 2020 version is available. (ver 10) * Only Joint that was imported as FBX to Marvelous Designer can be exported as FBX. 2. Import/Export FBX with multiple avatars (ver 12.2) * Multiple avatars can be imported or exported simultaneously using the FBX file format. 3. Export FBX with Material Names (Ver 2025.0) * Material Names are now synchronized exported with the FBX.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for importing and exporting FBX files, detailing the steps, settings, and options to effectively manage Geometry, Material, Joint, and Camera Animation data.

title: ZIPPER: Zipper Style
content: **New in 2025.1** Add Properties Assign Options **** Ability to easily manage and edit Zipper by style in the Object Browser. **** #### **Add** 1. Add a zipper style by clicking the Add button in the zipper tab of the object browser, or [create a zipper](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358168494745-ZIPPER-Create-Zippers) directly in the 3D window. → A zipper with the default style will be added. **📝Note:** _You can copy an existing zipper style with the same settings by clicking the**Copy** button._ #### **Properties** **Style** 1. Select the added style in the Zipper tab to set its properties. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Information** | Enter the zipper’s name. Each component of the zipper style, such as the chain, slider, puller, or stopper, can be named individually. **Function** | Set the zipper to be one-way or two-way. For two-way zippers, you can set the locking direction to either head-to-head or Bottom-to-Bottom. Changing the slider material will be applied identically to both sides. **Type** | Set the zipper type (Plastic, Nylon, Metal, etc.). **Specification** | Set the zipper gauge. The zipper width and the size of the slider, puller, and stopper can be adjusted individually **Save/Open** | Save or open the zipper style as a .ZPS file. → The changes will be applied to all 3D zippers using the selected style. **Each Component** Adjust chain, slider, and puller properties in more detail. 1. Click the corresponding chain, slider, puller, or stopper using the **Select/Move** tool. **• Select All** **** When you select one of the slider, puller, or stopper components, all related parts are selected at once. **• Select Component** If all components are currently selected, clicking one again will select only that component. **• Select Part of a Component** If a component consists of multiple meshes, clicking it again allows you to select a specific part. 2. Set selected component properties. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Chain** | **Length** | Adjust the length of the Zipper teeth. **Extend** (ver 2026.1) | Adjust the extend length and select the direction. **Particle Distance** | Adjust the particle distance of the zipper tape pattern. **Fold** | Adjust the Strength and Angle of the fold for Sewing between the Zipper and Pattern. **Physical Property** | Adjust physical properties of zipper tape pattern. **Slider/Puller/Stopper** | **Size/Weight** | Set the size and weight of each component individually. **Fasten** | Select the zip direction, and select a side of the zipper tape where the slider will locate when the zipper is open. **Material Type, Material** | Materials can be changed to each selected component, allowing for more diverse appearances. **Save/Open** | Save or open the zipper style as a .ZPS file. **** #### **Apply** 1.
